rationale: Round 1 built and passed correctness with no ICE fallback, so this round pushes more aggressively toward resistance: SecurityGain and DiversityGain are raised across the board (SUB highest, since arithmetic-heavy sieve bit-masking benefits most from instruction substitution; BCF and FLA next, to obscure the tight bit-sieve loops and the dispatch structure of the multi-benchmark main; SPLIT and IBR add cheap control-flow diversification with almost no runtime impact; ICALL and IGV stay moderate as they mainly hinder static analysis of the tiny 521-byte text where marginal benefit is smaller). RuntimeCost/SizeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low because nsieve-bits is a compute-bound benchmark whose hot loops are runtime-sensitive, the binary is already tiny so growth is tolerable but not free, and the program's correctness must be preserved; the modest BCF/FLA runtime weights still allow application where features indicate loops can absorb the transformation without exceeding acceptable overhead.
